correctness.rationale: Let s=x+y. On the (f,g) step, (s',x')=(2+f-g-s,2s-x-f); the four lower and four upper x-bounds follow from y∈[0,1/2], x'∈[1/2,1], y'∈[0,1], and x∈[0,1]. Pulling the intervals back for all 16 pairs and integrating their linear envelopes gives precisely AB, BA, AD, CA, each of area 1/48. The two recurrent words are repetitions of AB or BA; their two-step translation is -4δ about s=3/4 or 5/4. Intersecting translates of the respective two-letter interval takes the extreme shift in each bound and gives width 1/4-(4m-1)|δ| on |δ|≤1/[4(4m-1)]. The terminal AD constraint at ε=3/4-s intersects the initial AB interval with the last AD interval shifted by -4(m-1)ε. The initial CA constraint, in the ensuing A coordinates with Jacobian one, intersects the interval of the first CA step with the terminal A upper bound shifted by -4(m-1)ε. Both yield width min(2ε,1/4-(4m-3)ε) on 0≤ε≤1/[4(4m-3)]. These give recurrent areas 1/[16(4m-1)] and transient areas 1/[16(4m-1)(4m-3)] each. Summation and nested-set squeezing prove the frozen even formula and all-time normalizing constant. The frozen verification notes overstate the supplied main program: it checks 240 named word areas, including the four positive pairs at m=1, but does not enumerate all 16 pairs. That supplementary evidence error does not affect the independent full transition check or the symbolic proof.
residual_risks: The independent rational checks corroborate the algebra and do not substitute for the translated interval proof at arbitrary m.
